title: Setting Up Cloud Deception with GCP

blocks.text: This integration guide provides information on prerequisites and how to integrate Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with Zscaler Deception to set up Cloud Deception by deploying various GCP-specific decoy resources.
Before you set up Cloud Deception with GCP, ensure that you have:

blocks.item: Access to a GCP project with an Administrator role. If you do not have an Administrator role, ensure that your account has the minimum project-level IAM roles.
See instructions.

table: Enables the required Google Cloud APIs using the google_project_service resource.
Creates project-level IAM bindings and configures audit logging using the ProjectIamAuditConfig resource.
Creates service accounts for logging and decoy resources.
Creates service account keys used by the CMC for log polling and decoy lures. This role is required in addition to roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin.
Attaches service accounts to resources, such as the health-check function.
Creates and manages decoy buckets, logging buckets, storage objects, and bucket-level IAM permissions.
Grants the roles/logging.viewAccessor role on the _Default/_AllLogs log view.
Creates Secret Manager decoys and configures their IAM permissions.
Creates Artifact Registry decoys and configures their IAM permissions.
Creates Cloud SQL decoy instances and database users.

Required for private Cloud SQL decoys to read VPC network information. The Terraform deployment does not create the required network peering. Private Services Access, including the allocated IP address range and Service Networking peering, must already be configured for the project and network.
Required only if the deployer must configure Private Services Access for private Cloud SQL instances.

blocks.item: You can create a dedicated service account and assign the required project-level IAM roles to deploy Cloud Deception resources in GCP.
The account running the following commands must have permissions to create service accounts and modify project-level IAM policies.
To create a deployer service account:
Open the Google Cloud CLI (gcloud).
Run the following commands to specify your GCP project ID and the deployer service account name:
PROJECT=<customer-project-id> SA=zsd-deployer
Run the following command to create the deployer service account:
gcloud iam service-accounts create $SA \ --project=$PROJECT \ --display-name="ZS Deception deployer"
Run the following commands to assign the required project-level IAM roles to the deployer service account:

for role in \ serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin \ resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin \ iam.serviceAccountAdmin \ iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin \ iam.serviceAccountUser \ storage.admin \ cloudfunctions.developer \ logging.admin \ secretmanager.admin \ artifactregistry.admin \ cloudsql.admin do gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT \ --member="serviceAccount:$SA@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \ --role="roles/$role" done
These commands assign the IAM roles required to enable Google Cloud APIs and deploy and manage decoy resources.
Organization policies that do not hinder decoy deployment or operations:

Service account key creation: If your organization enforces the constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation constraint, the deployment fails because it cannot create the service account keys required for logging and decoy resources.

Public decoy buckets: If your organization enforces the constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains constraint, IAM bindings that grant the allUsers principal the roles/storage.objectViewer role on public-read buckets are rejected with error 412. Private buckets are unaffected.
Domain-restricted sharing: The same constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains constraint prevents the creation of decoys that require public ACL access.

blocks.text: During deployment, Terraform automatically enables the following Google Cloud APIs if they are not already enabled. These APIs support the deployment and management of decoy resources in your GCP project.

table: Manages project IAM permissions and audit configurations.
Manages service accounts, keys, and IAM bindings.
Provides access to log views and decoy audit logs.
Manages storage buckets for decoys, logging, and datasets.
Provides networking information for Cloud SQL decoys.
Enables Private Services Access for private Cloud SQL instances.

blocks.item: Removing the GCP decoys and associated project from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal removes the decoy resources through Terraform. However, the Google Cloud APIs enabled during deployment remain enabled.

When you deploy GCP decoys, the Deception Terraform stack enables Admin Activity and Data Access (DATA_READ, DATA_WRITE) audit logs only for the GCP services on which you have deployed decoys (i.e., cloud storage for bucket decoys, secret manager for secret decoys, artifact registry for repository decoys, and IAM for service-account decoys). The audit configuration for these services is managed by the stack. If you have existing Data Access audit settings for a service where a decoy is deployed, they are replaced by the stack's configuration.
Removing all decoys of a certain type, or decommissioning the deployment, removes the corresponding audit configuration and does not restore any previously configured settings.
Data Access logging can increase your Cloud Logging costs in proportion to activity on those services.

blocks.heading: Setting Up Cloud Deception with GCP

blocks.text: Follow these steps to set up Cloud Deception with GCP:

blocks.item: Step 1: Configure the Integration Between GCP and Deception
To integrate GCP with Deception:
Log in to the Deception Admin Portal.
Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Settings.
On the Settings page, click Add Project.
See image.
In the GCP Project Setting drawer:
Select Enabled.
Project ID: Enter the project ID of the GCP project to which you want to deploy the decoys.
Region: Select the region where you want to deploy the resources (i.e., health check function and logging bucket).
See image.
Click Save.
Locate the GCP project you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the gcp-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the gcp-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of a Google Cloud Storage bucket-based Terraform back end:
{ "terraform": { "backend": { "gcs": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "prefix": "deception/terraform" } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same GCP project.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and set the user agent for Terraform:
export TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT="<value_from_ui>"
Run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed.
Run the following command to export the state file as JSON:
terraform output -json gcp_terraform_output > deployment-output.json
The JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings, locate the GCP project you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.

Upon successful deployment, all necessary resources are created in GCP, and the information is updated in the Deception Admin Portal. The deployment also includes a health function app that polls the GCP account every 15 minutes to check and update the health status of the deployed decoys. blocks.item: Step 2: Configure the GCP Decoys
After successful integration of GCP with Deception, you can deploy various GCP-specific decoy resources. To learn how to configure the GCP decoys, see:
Service Account Decoys
Cloud Storage Decoys
Cloud SQL Decoys
Secret Manager Decoys
Artifact Registry Decoys
Step 3: Configure Lures Using GCP Decoys
After deploying the necessary decoys based on your requirements, you can configure the lures for the decoys. To learn how to configure lures using GCP decoys, see Configuring Lures Using GCP Decoys.
